verdict.root_cause: cartservice logged an orderly shutdown at 07:32:07 and emitted nothing afterwards [tr_1c560b1a85f8], one second before the change log records an image-reference update on cartservice to the hotfix tag — the change closest to onset and part of a repeated apply/revert pattern [tr_cdb7d79ee86d]. The replacement never returned to service: frontend's checkout cart-fetch fails at dial time because the cartservice name cannot be resolved, yielding gRPC UNAVAILABLE through 07:37 [tr_73550957ecc8]. frontend and checkoutservice are reporters, not origins — neither shows an in-window error surge or its own error logs [tr_a4cbbcb77d0e, tr_d5c4828b2878, tr_682848952546], and no change is recorded against checkoutservice [tr_f5f9b7ddcc35]. The other cartservice fault vectors (REDIS_ADDR override, egress-delay sidecar) were reverted 56m and ~1.2h before onset [tr_cdb7d79ee86d].
verdict.reasoning: The image swap at 07:32:08 and the cartservice shutdown at 07:32:07 coincide to the second [tr_cdb7d79ee86d, tr_1c560b1a85f8], and no startup banner or request line follows. The caller-side symptom is name-resolution failure before any connection exists [tr_73550957ecc8], which is what a vanished container looks like to the embedded resolver — not slowness and not backend errors. Because no RPC reaches cartservice, its call metrics stay empty [tr_f861cf7c2aeb] and callers' aggregate error ratios stay at or below baseline [tr_a4cbbcb77d0e, tr_d5c4828b2878, tr_682848952546]. The mechanism is a running artifact that is not the one that should be running, so reverting the image reference is the fix.
open_questions: Frontend code-14 errors already appear at ~07:12, before the shutdown and image swap, with no backend named [tr_73550957ecc8] — same fault with earlier onset, or unrelated spiky behaviour?
No container/pod status, restart count, or image-pull result was collected for the hotfix tag, so whether it failed to pull, failed to start, or failed health checks is unknown.
No direct DNS or service-discovery check was run, and eight services in the blast radius plus four unmeasured edges were never dispatched against.

alternatives.root_cause: An automated chaos harness deliberately stopped cartservice, and the outage is the injected condition rather than a defective artifact.
alternatives.why_not: Indistinguishable in mechanism and remedy from the primary verdict; it only reframes intent, and the recorded act at onset is still an image-reference change [tr_cdb7d79ee86d].

alternatives.root_cause: A service-discovery or DNS-layer fault independent of the deploy made cartservice unresolvable at roughly the same time.
alternatives.why_not: No DNS or service-name change is recorded [tr_cdb7d79ee86d], and cartservice's own logs show it stopping rather than merely becoming unreachable [tr_1c560b1a85f8].

proposal.expected_effect: Redeploying cartservice at its pre-07:32:08 image tag should bring a serving container back under the cart-service name. Observable as: the Loki stream {service="cart-service"}, silent since the 07:32:07 shutdown notice, resuming with a startup banner and AddItemAsync/GetCartAsync lines; and frontend's log stream ceasing to emit 'Error: 14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established' and the cartservice DNS-resolution failure at 127.0.0.11:53. Confirmation must come from logs: cartservice's Prometheus error-ratio series has no samples, and frontend's aggregate error ratio never rose above baseline.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if cart-service logs stay silent after five minutes (prior tag also fails to start, so the fault is platform or registry, not the hotfix image); or if cartservice logs return but frontend still reports the cartservice name unresolvable (service discovery, not the image). Also unexplained: frontend code-14 errors already at ~07:12, before the swap; if that band continues unchanged, the real mechanism is still unidentified. If the hotfix tag is re-applied minutes later, an automated harness is driving this and the action cannot hold.
proposal.risk: If the cause is DNS/service-discovery rather than the image, recreating the container re-registers the cart-service network alias and may extend the outage rather than end it. The recreate discards in-process cache state. The prior tag is inferred from the apply/revert pattern, not read directly; if it is itself an injected fault image, rollback restores a different broken state. No container status or image-pull result was ever collected, so this is a bet on the change, not a confirmed repair.
proposal.blast_radius: cartservice directly; frontend sees resets on the checkout cart-fetch edge already failing, and checkoutservice's order path through it. Both are currently within baseline error ratios, so a botched recreate would make their signals worse, not better.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts on frontend and checkoutservice within seconds of each other, with loadgenerator affected too, indicate a real user-facing failure rather than a quiet warning. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the alert pattern alone doesn't distinguish a bad deploy from a downstream dependency issue.
